title.narrative: Intermon Chad - Déné Ass: Women Can (R)

description.narrative:
Since 2016, Oxfam and its partners have been working to improve land access for vulnerable groups, especially women and youth, in regions such as Moyen-Chari, Mandoul, and Logone Oriental. They have helped allocate over 10,000 hectares of land to local cooperatives, empowering women and youth in the process. However, agricultural growth in these areas remains constrained by a lack of investment, outdated farming practices, and limited access to seeds and resources. While progress has been made, major issues such as land insecurity, inadequate infrastructure, and underdeveloped farming systems continue to hinder sustainable development and economic empowerment in Chad, particularly for women.
This new project aims to maximize the potential of this landby empowering 15 women and youth cooperatives, strengthening their leadership skills, and promoting economic independence. The goal is to enhance the economic power of these groups through the development of their entrepreneurship and advocacy capacities,as well as the local value chains for sesame, peanuts, and rice. Additionally, the project will focus on improving the production and commercialization of certified cereal and pulse seeds tailored to the specific needs of these regions. It will also support women and youth cooperatives in advancing the processing and marketing of agricultural products.
1. Sustainable Seed Production In the three regions, farmers often struggle toaccess high-quality, certified seeds, which are essential for improvingcrop yields. This project aims to establish a sustainable seed production system within the community. By working with local seed producers, we will provide training on modern farming techniques and help create certified seed groups that can supply seedstoother farmers. These groups will gradually become self-sufficient, and professional as seed providers reducing their reliance on external aid and ensuring the community has a consistent, reliable source of quality seeds.
2. Strengthening Local Cooperatives Many farmers in the three regions belong to small cooperatives, but these organizations often lack the resources and skills to grow their impact. This project will offer training and hands-on support to help these cooperatives strengthen their internal structures and functioning. Members will receive training in leadership, group dynamics, financial management, and creating business plans. We will also help equip cooperatives with tools for agricultural production and processing, allowing them to increase both the quality and quantity of their crops. Support will also go to building their marketintelligence with good networking and negotiation capacities. The goal is to create stronger, more resilient cooperatives that can better support theirmembers with marketing activities through facilitating the access to inputs, credits, and to product markets.
3. Enhancing Market Access for Local Farmers Access to markets is a major challenge for many farmers in the three regions, who often struggle to sell their crops at fair prices. This project will help cooperatives build relationships with local and regional buyers by developing a more organized and efficient market system. Farmers will receive guidance on how to connect with financial institutionsfor credit, and we will work to ensure they can negotiate better deals for their products. By creating stronger market links, we aim to increase the income of farmers and ensure they have a stable, reliable place to sell their goods.
4. Empowering Womenand Youth Through Leadership In the three regions, women and young people are often left out of key decisions about land and agriculture. This project will focus on strengthening the leadership roles of women and youth within the cooperatives. Wewill provide training on leadership, business management, and conflict resolution, so that they can take on active roles in decision-making processes. This empowerment will not only improve the role of women and youth in the community but also help them build theskills they need to succeed as entrepreneurs and leaders.
5. Advocacy for Women's Land and Economic Rights A crucial part of this project will be advocatingfor women and youth to have equal access to land and economic opportunities. In thethree regions, women often face significant barriers when it comes to land rights and access to agricultural resources. Through this project, we will work with local authorities and traditional leaders to push for policies that support women’s land rights and ensure that women and young people can participate fully in the economy. We will also advocate for improvements in business conditions and the certification process to sup-port local farmers.

participating-org.narrative: Oxfam Intermón is since 1997 a member of the international Oxfam confederation, sharing values and a strategic plan to achieve greater global impact. Intermón Oxfam fights, with and for disadvantaged populations and as part of a broad global movement, with the aim of eradicating injustice and poverty, and to ensure that all human beings can fully exercise their rights and enjoy a dignified life. Mission, Vision and Values are the components of Oxfam Intermón identity and guide its steps as an organisation and the ideal with which Oxfam Intermón wants to live in order to obtain a fairer world with greater solidarity.
